neighbours.label: object pronoun after a motion verb + 'to' (came to me, walked to him): moving toward a person
fire: When the puppy got scared, it ran straight to me.
After the accident his sister hurried over to him.
Late that night, an old friend came to me with a strange story.
The child stumbled, and her father rushed to her.
Whenever she needed advice, she would go to him first.
The villagers brought the sick boy to me at dawn.
The stray cat slowly walked to us across the yard.
He was lost, so the guide came back to him.
quiet: When the puppy got scared, it ran straight to the porch.
After the accident his sister hurried over to the hospital.
Late that night, an old friend came by with a strange story.
The child stumbled, and her father rushed to the gate.
Whenever she needed advice, she would go to the library first.
The villagers brought the sick boy to the clinic at dawn.
The stray cat slowly walked to the fence across the yard.
He was lost, so the guide came back to the trail.

notes: Card: ' him' x6, ' me' x5 in 'should've gone to him', 'walked to him', 'came to me', 'brought a youth to me', 'Venga a nosotros'. - pole: passengers.
